index.html.purpose: The public front door of the studio. It introduces the practice to a parent who has never met you, states the core promise — independent progress that a parent can actually see — and drives two actions: sign in, or request a place.
index.html.audience: Anyone on the internet. No sign-in required.
index.html.why: This is the page that converts a stranger into an enquiry. It is also the page search engines rank, so it carries the studio's structured data and social preview.
how: Read the promise and the proof statistics.
Click Sign in to portal if you already have an account.
Click Request a place to submit an application — it takes about two minutes.
Accept the install prompt to add the studio to your home screen.
index.html.connects: Feeds login.html and apply.html, and links out to the HMG Concepts ecosystem in the footer.

login.html.purpose: The single entry point to the private portal. It signs in parents, learners, tutors and admins, and offers password recovery and a route to apply.
login.html.why: Every privacy guarantee in the product begins here. The role attached to your account decides what the database will and will not return for the rest of your session.
how: Enter your email — or a learner's student ID such as TC-0001 — and your password.
Use Forgot password to get a secure reset link by email.
New families should use Apply instead; accounts require admin approval before they open.
After sign-in you land on the dashboard built for your role.
login.html.connects: The gateway to every protected page. Each sign-in and sign-out is written to the login audit trail.

dashboard.html.purpose: Your personalised home screen, and the most role-aware page in the studio. An owner sees studio-wide KPIs, cash position and at-risk learners. A tutor sees today's classes, attendance to mark and work to grade. A parent sees the next class, the latest scores and the balance owing. A learner sees homework, reading and quizzes due.
dashboard.html.audience: Every signed-in role — the same URL renders a completely different page per role.
dashboard.html.why: It is the daily habit that keeps families engaged. A parent who opens this page each week and sees movement is a parent who renews.
how: Read the KPI tiles across the top for the headline position.
Use the quick-link tiles to jump straight into a module.
Check the alert strip for at-risk learners, unpaid invoices or an hour bank about to run dry.
Open the bell for anything new since your last visit.
dashboard.html.connects: The hub of the entire studio — it links to every module that has been enabled.

about.html.purpose: Explains who runs the studio, the teaching philosophy and the track record. A credibility page for a parent comparing two or three tutors before committing.
about.html.why: Tutoring is a trust purchase. Parents read this page before they read your prices.
how: Read the studio story, the approach and the credentials.
Follow the call to action to apply or sign in.
about.html.connects: Linked from the landing page and every footer; indexed for search.

contact.html.purpose: Every way to reach the studio — WhatsApp, email, phone and social — plus an enquiry form that lands directly in the staff CRM.
contact.html.why: A parent who cannot reach you in under a minute contacts the next tutor on their list.
how: Choose the channel you prefer; WhatsApp and email open your own device app.
Or submit the form and the studio replies from the Inquiries board.
contact.html.connects: Writes to the inquiries table, which staff triage in the Inquiries/CRM module.

forgot-password.html.purpose: Sends a secure password-reset link by email through Supabase Auth. Nobody at the studio can see or set your password.
forgot-password.html.audience: Anyone locked out of their account.
forgot-password.html.why: Self-service recovery keeps the admin out of the credential business entirely, which is both safer and less work.
how: Type the email address on your account.
Open the email and click the link — it expires shortly.
Choose a new password; the strength meter shows you when it is strong enough.

change-password.html.purpose: Change your password while signed in, with a live strength meter that scores length, case mixing, digits and symbols.
change-password.html.why: Shared family devices are common. A periodic password change, plus the idle auto-lock, is what keeps a portal safe on a household laptop.
how: Enter your current password, then the new one twice.
Aim for Strong or Very strong on the meter.
Save — you remain signed in on this device.
change-password.html.connects: The security guard records the change in the login audit trail.

install.html.purpose: A complete, illustrated walkthrough for installing the studio as a real app on iPhone, Android, Windows, macOS and Chromebook — including what you gain by doing it.
install.html.why: Installed users open the portal far more often, and only an installed app can deliver class reminders when the browser tab is closed.
how: Find your device in the list.
Follow the numbered steps for that platform.
Confirm the studio icon has appeared on your home screen or dock.
Allow notifications when asked, so reminders can reach you.
install.html.connects: Backed by manifest.json and sw.js, and reinforced by the install banner that appears across the platform.

offline.html.purpose: The friendly page the service worker serves when the device loses connection, so a family on poor mobile data never sees a raw browser error.
offline.html.why: Intermittent connectivity is normal for the studio's audience. Failing gracefully is the difference between 'the network dropped' and 'this app is broken'.
how: Reconnect, then press retry.
Pages you have already visited still open from the offline cache.
offline.html.connects: Served automatically by sw.js whenever a navigation request fails.

developer.html.purpose: Credits the build, documents the technology stack and the design constraints, and links to HMG Technologies for studios wanting bespoke work.
developer.html.why: Transparency about the stack is part of the pitch: no vendor lock-in, no recurring platform fee, and the client owns the source.
how: Read the architecture and constraint summary.
Follow the ecosystem links to the wider HMG network.
developer.html.connects: Part of the HMG Concepts ecosystem link graph, which is also how the sites reinforce each other for search.

site-index.html.purpose: A complete, human-readable index of every page in the studio, grouped by function — the fastest way to find a module when you know what it is called but not where it lives.
site-index.html.why: With well over a hundred modules enabled, browsing beats hunting through a nav tree.
how: Scan the groups, or press Ctrl/Cmd+F and type what you want.
Click straight through to the module.
site-index.html.connects: The human counterpart to sitemap.xml, which is the machine version search engines read.

builder.html.purpose: The internal HMG wizard that generates a complete, branded studio for a client: studio name, logo, theme, font, layout, modules and optional Supabase keys, then produces a ready-to-deploy ZIP with a one-click SQL schema.
builder.html.audience: HMG representatives only — this page is never shipped inside a client build.
builder.html.why: It is the factory. Every client studio in existence is stamped out of this one page, which is why its output has to be complete and correct.
how: Work through the wizard step by step.
Preview the chosen theme, font and layout live before committing.
Download the ZIP, then follow DEPLOYMENT-GUIDE.md exactly.
Run database/complete-schema.sql in a fresh Supabase project and promote the first admin.
builder.html.connects: Generator-only. It reads the same page files the client will receive, so what you preview is what they get.

family-links.html.purpose: Connect a parent to the child or children they are responsible for. This single mapping is what switches the family portal on: once linked, a parent sees that child's classes, scores, reading, invoices and messages — and nothing about anyone else's child.
family-links.html.audience: Owner, admin and tutors who handle enrolment.
family-links.html.why: An unlinked child is invisible to their parent, and a parent record with no portal login cannot sign in at all. Those two gaps are the reason almost every family says "I can't see anything", and this page finds both for you automatically.
how: Pick the parent, pick the learner, choose the relationship, press Link them.
Read the Needs attention panel — it lists learners with no parent and parents with no portal login.
For a parent with no login: have them sign up, approve them on Approvals, then attach their account here.
Remove a link with the × beside a child; the parent stops seeing them immediately.
family-links.html.connects: Writes parent_learner, which is what the is_parent_of() database rule reads. Pairs with My children, Approvals and Learners.

my-children.html.purpose: A parent's home page: one card per child showing the next class with date, time and duration, the latest scores by subject, attendance, hours left in the bank, and the reading set before the next lesson.
my-children.html.audience: Parents and guardians. Staff see the same layout for the learners they teach.
my-children.html.why: This is the page that delivers the studio's promise — independent progress a parent can actually see. A parent who opens this weekly and sees movement renews.
how: Each card is one child. Read the four headline tiles first.
Use Next classes to confirm the date, time and duration you agreed.
Open the full scoresheet for the detail behind any score.
If you see no children at all, the studio has not linked you yet — the page tells you exactly what to ask for.
my-children.html.connects: Reads learners, scoresheet, sessions, attendance and reading, all filtered by Row Level Security. Fed by Family links.

wallet.html.purpose: A prepaid credit account for every family. A parent pays once for a block of lessons or a sum of money, and each attended session is drawn down from that balance automatically. Every movement is a permanent ledger row, so the balance is always the sum of its history and can never quietly drift.
wallet.html.audience: Owner, admin and staff can top up and inspect any family's wallet. A signed-in parent sees only their own balance and movements, enforced by row-level security in the database rather than by hiding a button.
wallet.html.why: Chasing an invoice after the lesson has already been taught is the weakest position a tutoring studio can be in. A prepaid wallet reverses the cash flow — the money arrives first and the teaching draws it down. It is the feature the market leader builds its entire billing around, and it is reported to lift monthly renewals by up to 42% because families top up before they run out instead of being chased afterwards.
how: Switch the wallet on in Settings and set the low-balance threshold that puts a family on the chase list.
Choose a family from the dropdown — it fills itself from your parents list, so there is nothing to type.
Enter the amount received and the bank reference, then press Add credit.
Pick the unit: Currency holds money, Sessions holds a number of lessons. Studios with one fixed lesson price usually prefer sessions.
Teach as normal. Marking a learner present on the Attendance page deducts the session automatically.
Work the Low balances list weekly — each family has a one-tap WhatsApp link.
To correct a mistake, add a reversing entry rather than editing history. That is what keeps the ledger auditable.
wallet.html.connects: Deducts automatically from attendance.html. Feeds invoices.html and payment-plans.html. Balances appear to families in my-children.html. Thresholds are configured in settings.html.

payment-plans.html.purpose: Splits a large fee into an instalment schedule and tracks every part of it. You enter the total, the number of instalments and how often they fall due; every date and amount is generated for you.
payment-plans.html.audience: Owner, admin and staff. A parent sees their own plan in the family portal, read-only.
payment-plans.html.why: Termly fees are routinely paid in parts, and a family who cannot pay ₦180,000 at once will happily pay ₦60,000 three times. Every serious competitor offers instalments; without this the conversation happened in WhatsApp and the tracking lived in somebody's head. The arrears list replaces that.
how: Choose the family and, optionally, the learner. Both lists auto-fill.
Enter the total owed — not the instalment amount. The split is calculated for you and previewed live as you type.
Choose how many instalments and how often: weekly, fortnightly, monthly or termly.
Press Generate schedule. Every due date and amount is created in one action.
Note that rounding is absorbed by the first instalment, never the last, so a family never meets a surprise odd amount at the end of a plan they had budgeted for.
Press ✓ Mark paid on an instalment as the money arrives; today's date is filled in for you.
Anything past its due date appears in Arrears with the number of days late.
payment-plans.html.connects: Sits alongside invoices.html and payments.html. Families with a wallet can draw instalments from wallet.html. Sibling discounts configured in settings.html apply to the family statement.

security-centre.html.purpose: The studio's safety console. It shows what an anonymous stranger can reach, who has been touching learner records, failed sign-in attempts, the consent you hold and the data requests families have made. It also produces the two documents a regulator or a worried parent will ask for: a complete export of everything held on one learner, and an anonymised export for analytics.
security-centre.html.audience: Owner and administrator only. Every function behind this page re-checks your role inside the database, so it cannot be reached by editing the page in a browser.
security-centre.html.why: You hold children's names, dates of birth, guardian phone numbers, addresses, exam scores and safeguarding notes. Nigeria's NDPA 2023 gives families the right to see and correct that data, and the same duty exists under GDPR and FERPA elsewhere. The control every one of those regimes names first is an immutable audit trail — a record of who accessed what that the accessor cannot edit or delete.
how: Press Run security scan. It asks the database what an anonymous visitor can reach; everything listed should be something a stranger is supposed to use.
Confirm Tables without row-level security is empty. Anything listed there is readable by anyone holding the public key, which is printed in your page source.
Review failed sign-ins. Three or more failures against one address is either a forgotten password or somebody guessing.
Use the Audit trail to answer "who changed this?" — filter by table and record id and read the before-and-after of every field.
When a family asks what you hold on their child, use Export a learner's full record. The statutory deadline is 30 days here and 45 under FERPA; this takes seconds.
Log every request in Data requests so the clock is visible and nothing is missed.
Record photo, trip and marketing permissions in Consent, storing the signed form as a Drive link — this studio never accepts uploads.
security-centre.html.connects: Reads the same audit trail shown in activity-log.html. Works with safeguarding.html, compliance.html and policies.html. Licence state is managed in license.html.

cbt-results.html.purpose: Every quiz and exam the studio has set, each with a Results button. Open one and you see who sat it — registered learners and anonymous candidates who used only a code — what they scored, how long they took, and any integrity flags. Open a single sitting and you see exactly what that candidate did: every question, the answer given, the answer expected, the mark awarded, and a timeline of anything the anti-cheat layer noticed.
cbt-results.html.audience: Owner, admin and tutors. Families never reach this page; the database refuses it by role rather than merely hiding the link.
cbt-results.html.why: A score on its own tells you almost nothing. Item analysis tells you whether the class failed a question or the question failed the class — a facility below 25% usually means a wrong answer key, not thirty confused learners. Catching that before you publish a grade is the difference between a defensible mark and an argument with a parent.
how: The table lists every paper with sittings, how many are unreviewed, and the class average.
Press 📊 Results beside a paper to open its results.
Scan the summary strip: sat, average, highest, lowest, flagged, unreviewed, median time.
Press 🔍 Audit on any row to see that candidate's full paper, question by question, with their answer beside the expected one.
Use 🧪 Item analysis to find questions the whole class failed. Anything marked CHECK THE KEY should be verified before you release marks.
Override a mark with ✏️ Review — essays and code are marked by keyword and always need a human eye. The original machine score is kept beside yours.
Live submissions appear automatically every 30 seconds; each links straight to the result.
Export any result set to CSV for a mark book or a parent meeting.
cbt-results.html.connects: Papers are built in cbt-multi.html and sat in cbt-exam.html. Learners see their own review in cbt-review.html. Graded results push to scoresheet.html. Submission alerts also appear in notifications.html.
